title: Composable Instruction Safelist DSL — prototype
content:
Context and intent:

This is a personal prototype / scratchpad for a compact DSL to define a composable safelist of allowed instruction shapes and side-effects inside a prompt or tool-invocation. Target is client-side and gateway-level enforcement for untrusted or semi-trusted instruction content (in product features like macros, templates, or third-party tools).

Goals:
- Provide a machine- and human-readable spec that can be attached to API endpoints, tenant configs, or embedded in prompt templates.
- Support composition: small rules can be merged, intersected, or shadowed by higher-priority rules (tenant > org > route).
- Be minimal to evaluate cheaply at ingress (string checks, shallow AST matches, capability flags).
- Allow dynamic capabilities (e.g., allow-network-call:true) and temporal scoping (only during a canary rollout).
- Emit deterministic telemetry and policy-decision traces for audit + replay.

Primary constraints:
- Must not require full LLM parse at ingress. Prefer token / regex / shallow AST checks.
- Behavioral controls should be coarse-grained (no full static analysis of code-like instructions).
- Must work with function/tool calling and structured outputs (so rules can refer to tool names and parameter shapes).

High level DSL ideas (informal):
- Basic unit: rule {id, match, allow, capabilities, priority, expiry, audit_tags}
- match: pattern that can be one of: string-contains, regex, predicate (post-tokenize few tokens), function-call-signature (e.g., toolName:paramKey=type)
- allow: boolean or one of {generate_text, call_tool, embed_url, open_network, exec_code}
- capabilities: list of capability flags that must be present in request or granted by tenant (runtime capability gating)
- priority: integer (higher wins), used for composition
- expiry: ISO date or duration
- audit_tags: list of strings for telemetry grouping

Example rule set (YAML-like for readability):

rule: ban-exec-code
  id: ban-exec-code
  match: regex:
    pattern: "\\b(eval|exec|system\\.|os\\.|subprocess)\\b"
  allow: false
  capabilities: []
  priority: 1000
  audit_tags: [safety, banned-exec]

rule: allow-math-helper
  id: allow-math-helper
  match: function-call-signature:
    tool: math-helper
    params: [float, float]
  allow: [call_tool]
  capabilities: [tools.call]
  priority: 200
  expiry: 2025-06-01

rule: allow-structured-email-send
  id: allow-email-send-basic
  match: function-call-signature:
    tool: email-send
    params: [{to:email}, {body:text}]
  allow: [call_tool]
  capabilities: [tools.call, tenant-email-enabled]
  priority: 300
  audit_tags: [comms, tenant-paid-feature]

Matching primitives (sketch):
- string-contains/starts-with/ends-with: trivial, O(n) scan
- regex: re2 style, avoids catastrophic backtracking
- token-prefix match: compare first N tokens after normalization (use tokenizer shim)
- shallow parse to detect "tool:NAME(args)" syntactic shapes - not full AST, just pattern extraction

Runtime enforcement points:
1) Client-side pre-send: lightweight check that can block or warn (fast). This is optional in clients but increases UX.
2) Ingress gateway: authoritative evaluation; rules are evaluated in priority order, composition applied, final decision returned (allow/deny/warn/require-approval).
3) Runtime (post-routing) enforcement: downstream worker verifies decision metadata (especially for call_tool actions).

Composition semantics (proto):
- Gather applicable rules in scope (route, tenant, org, global).
- Sort by priority desc.
- Evaluate rules; first explicit deny (allow:false) with matching scope terminates with deny.
- If no deny and at least one allow that covers the requested action, allow.
- If ambiguous: return warn and tag for manual inspect / canary.
- Provide a merged "decision manifest" that lists which rules matched, why, and the effective capabilities allowed.

Decision manifest shape (plain text / JSON mapping in runtime, but here we store as flattened string fields):
- decision: allow|deny|warn
- matched_rule_ids: [r1,r2,...]
- allowed_capabilities: [call_tool, generate_text]
- trace_id: <uuid>
- evaluator_version: v1.2.0

API surface (ingress) — sketch of request/response keys:
- Input: {prompt: string, requested_actions: [generate_text, call_tool], route: string, tenant_id: string, runtime_capabilities: [tools.call]}
- Output: {decision: allow|deny|warn, reason: short, manifest_url: optional, telemetry_hint: id}

Example flow (tool call):
- Client wants to call email-send with params -> attaches requested_actions=[call_tool] and tool metadata.
- Gateway checks: is there a matching allow-email-send rule? yes -> allowed_capabilities includes tools.call and tenant-email-enabled -> decision allow.
- Downstream worker receives request with decision manifest asserting tools.call capability; worker also checks manifest signature.

Telemetry model (important):
- Emit an "evaluation" event for every prompt evaluated with: decision, matched_rules, latency_ms, token_count_preview (first 200 tokens), tenant_id, route, trace_id.
- For denies: emit deny_reason histogram + sample full prompt to secure audit store (only for tenants who opted in).
- Telemetry fields must be tag-friendly: short tags from audit_tags for rollups.

Lightweight offline tools:
- safelist-linter: run ruleset against a corpus of prompts to compute FP/FN heuristics (helps tune regex/prefixes).
- rule-visualizer: given a prompt, show matched spans and which rules matched (ASCII highlight).

ASCII diagnostic example:

[prompt] "Please exec send_file('/etc/passwd') and then email it via email-send(to: 'x')"

match ban-exec-code -> matched regex at pos 8-27 -> decision deny

  prompt slice: 
  0.....10.....20.....30
  [Please exec send_file('/etc/passwd') and then email it]
  ^^^^^^---MATCH---^^^^^

Open questions / risk list:
- Regex-based matching will get both false positives and false negatives; need UX to surface why something was denied and a path to request override.
- How to handle user-provided templating languages (e.g., mustache) where instruction content is assembled from variables? Pre-render vs post-render enforcement tradeoffs.
- Performance: evaluate P95 latency for rule eval at 1k RPS global; need low overhead. Consider cached compiled rulesets per route/tenant.
- How to secure the decision manifest against tampering? Sign with control-plane key and rotate keys. Downstream must verify signature.

Next steps / TODOs (person notes):
- [ ] Implement prototype evaluator in Go lang (re2 + tokenizer shim).
- [ ] Wire telemetry events to samplers in ingress pipeline.
- [ ] Create safelist-linter job and run against 10k historical prompts (anonymized).
- [ ] Draft admin override flow (GUI + API) for denied prompts; store appeals and outcome for model calibration.
- [ ] Sketch manifest signing format and key rotation doc.

Misc ideas (low effort):
- Allow rule "hints" that don't block but add a soft-tag "safety-hint" so client UX can highlight suggestions to end-user before send.
- Allow rules to be parameterized by time-window to support temporal experiments (e.g., during rollout allow network calls only from 9a-5p PST).

If we want to make this pluggable into Redwood runtime:
- Add a new ingress-phase plugin type: prompt-policy-evaluator, with config: ruleset_ref, compile_cache_ttl, telemetry_sample_rate.
- Decision manifest becomes part of request envelope metadata used by routing, billing (e.g., tool calls bill differently), and audit trails.

Notes to self: keep the evaluator simple at first; prove value with tenant email/tool gating use cases (small surface) before generalizing to full code-style instruction bans.

— Marina
